title: Development of a DIY rehabilitation device for lower limb weakness in acute to subacute ischemic stroke
author: Tangmanee, Muengtaweepongsa, et al.
materials: A patient had a significant communication defect.2.3.2.

steps.title: Design device geometry in SolidWorks
steps.instruction: Using SolidWorks, model a lower‑limb rehabilitation machine that can operate on either left or right limbs and reproduces hip lift‑up, hip flexion‑extension, knee flexion‑extension, and ankle dorsiflexion‑plantarflexion as illustrated in Fig. 1.

steps.title: Calculate patient forces for limb segments
steps.instruction:
Assume a patient weight of up to 80 kg and height ≈170 cm. Compute forces for each segment using F = (%bodyweight) × (bodymass) × g (9.81 m·s⁻²):
- Femur: 0.1447 × 80 kg × 9.81 = 113.5606 N
- Trunk: 0.4302 × 80 kg × 9.81 = 337.621 N
- Tibia: 0.0457 × 80 kg × 9.81 = 35.8654 N
- Foot: 0.0133 × 80 kg × 9.81 = 10.4378 N

steps.title: Compute motor torque for hip‑knee flexion
steps.instruction:
For the hip‑knee flexion‑extension exercise, solve the free‑body diagram (Fig. 2, Fig. 3):
- ΣM = 0 ⇒ (F_strap)(L_hip_strap) – (F_femur)(L_hip_femur) = 0
- With L_hip_strap = 0.23 m, F_femur = 113.5606 N, L_hip_femur = 0.1752 m, obtain F_strap = 86.5036 N.
- Motor torque τ_motor = F_strap × (L_hip – strap) = 86.5036 N × 0.23 m = 19.8958 N·m.

steps.title: Compute motor torque for hip bridging
steps.instruction:
For hip‑lifting (bridging):
- Calculate hip‑raise angle θ = arcsin(0.4323/1.045) = 24.4365°.
- Solve the system of equations (1)–(5) to obtain F_strap = –232.1225 N (magnitude 232.1225 N).
- Motor torque τ_motor = F_strap × 0.23 m = 53.3882 N·m.

steps.title: Compute motor torque for ankle dorsiflexion
steps.instruction:
Assume foot drop of 30° while supine, giving ankle angle θ = 90° – 30° = 60°.
- Let x = L_foot/2 = 0.0633 m.
- From ΣM = 0: (F_motor)(l_ankle_heel) = F_foot cos θ × x → F_motor = (10.4378 N × cos 60°) / 0.0723 m = 84.5692 N.
- Motor torque τ_motor = F_motor × 0.0723 m = 0.3304 N·m.

steps.title: Apply safety factor and select motors
steps.instruction:
Multiply each calculated torque by a safety factor of 1.5:
- Hip‑knee flexion: 19.8958 N·m × 1.5 = 29.8437 N·m → select motor ≈30 N·m.
- Hip bridging: 53.3882 N·m × 1.5 = 80.0823 N·m → select motor ≈81 N·m.
- Ankle dorsiflexion: 0.3304 N·m × 1.5 = 0.4955 N·m → select motor ≈0.5 N·m.

steps.title: Assemble regeneration circuit
steps.instruction: Wire the lower‑limb rehabilitation machine according to the control circuit shown in Fig. 6, ensuring proper connections for the three electric motors and safety interlocks.

steps.title: Screen participants according to criteria
steps.instruction: Enroll acute ischemic stroke patients (onset ≤3 months) meeting all inclusion criteria: age 40–80 yr, TMSE > 22, NIHSS 5–15, Brunstrom stage > 1, consent obtained. Exclude any with: complete sensory loss, significant communication defect, non‑stroke weakness (e.g., Parkinson’s, spinal injury), heart/lung disease, joint deformity/inflammation, visual NIHSS = 3, or sensory NIHSS = 2.

steps.title: Randomize eligible patients into groups
steps.instruction: Using a computer‑generated randomization schedule, allocate the 20 participants who complete the 12‑week trial equally (10 per group) into an experimental group (prototype device) and a control group (standard therapy only).

steps.title: Conduct rehabilitation sessions
steps.instruction:
For both groups, deliver 30 min of standard rehabilitation daily, five days per week, for three months. Additionally:
- Experimental group: 30 min of exercise with the prototype device (hip flexion‑extension, knee flexion‑extension, ankle dorsiflexion‑plantarflexion, and hip bridging) as shown in Fig. 7.
- Control group: 30 min of focused exercises (same movements) without the device.
Maintain ROM limits: hip/knee 0°–80°, ankle 0°–60°, and hip‑bridge lift height 15 cm. Do not apply the device to patients with complete sensation loss to avoid bruises or heel injury.

steps.title: Measure outcomes at scheduled intervals
steps.instruction: Assess each participant using the Fugl‑Meyer Assessment for lower extremity (FMA‑LE), Brunstrom Stage of Motor Recovery (lower extremity), and modified Rankin Scale (mRS) at baseline (before treatment) and after weeks 2, 4, 8, and 12. Record all scores for subsequent statistical analysis (one‑way repeated measures ANOVA, paired t‑tests, significance p < 0.05).
